heading: INT. LONG-TERM CARE HOME - PRIVATE ROOM - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. LONG-TERM CARE HOME - PRIVATE ROOM - LATE AFTERNOON
A single bed, neatly made.
A rocking chair by the window.
A tray of untouched dinner on the side table.
Photographs crowd the dresser: a wedding, a fishing trip, a toddler on a pony.
The window frames a brick wall and a sliver of sky.
AUGUSTUS "GUS" WELLINGTON-ABARA, 80s, in a cardigan and slippers, sits in the rocking chair with a landline phone in his lap.
The cord stretches to the wall.
He stares at the receiver as if it might speak first.
He lifts it.
Dials slowly, one number at a time, with a shaky forefinger.
It rings.
Hello?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Hello. Is this Daniel?
units.name: GUS

units.text: Who's calling?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: It's your father.
units.name: GUS

units.text: A long pause on the line.
Gus watches the brick wall.
A pigeon lands on the sill, ruffles its feathers, takes off again.
Dad. It's been a while.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: It has.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Is something wrong?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: No. I just wanted to hear your voice.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Silence.
Gus sets the dinner tray aside, lifts the cover.
Cold peas.
He puts the cover back.
I can't talk long. I'm at work.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Of course. I understand.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Is the staff treating you well?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: They are very kind.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Good.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Gus rocks.
The chair creaks.
He runs his thumb along the phone cord, back and forth.
I found your old baseball glove.
units.name: GUS

units.text: You kept that?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: In the closet. It still smells like leather.
units.name: GUS

units.text: God. I haven't thought about that in years.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: You pitched a shutout in it. Nineteen eighty-four.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Eighty-five.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Eighty-five.
units.name: GUS

units.text: He smiles, and his eyes go to the dresser, to a faded photograph of a small boy in an oversized cap, scowling at the camera.
He picks up the frame, wipes the glass with his sleeve.
Dad, I really have to go.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Yes. Of course. Thank you for answering.
units.name: GUS

units.text: I'll call you Sunday.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: I'd like that.
units.name: GUS

units.text: The line clicks.
He holds the receiver against his ear a moment longer, listening to the empty hum.
He puts the phone down gently on its cradle.
Sets the photograph back on the dresser, straightens it.
He crosses to the window and stands there, hands clasped behind his back, looking at the brick.
After a while, he sits again in the rocking chair, takes the cold fork from the tray, and begins, slowly, to eat the peas.
